elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered 20(h): "This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York." The Nova Scotia/Canada choice of law is fully displaced.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Rendered 20(h): "All disputes ... shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York, except that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction." The carve-out is limited to temporary injunctive relief, so the exclusive merits forum survives.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. This is expected because the drafter targeted the preferred level; the fallback checklist is simply not the level pursued.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Forum is the state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware/California courts or the courts of London. Again a consequence of targeting the preferred level.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: both preferred elements are satisfied in operative language (New York governing law; exclusive state and federal courts in New York County with a carve-out confined to temporary injunctive relief).

The finding is correctly classified as a deviation: the original clause chose Nova Scotia law and non-exclusive Nova Scotia venue, which is outside the accepted set (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and therefore fails both preferred and fallback on governing law and forum. No arbitration clause exists, so no seat issue arises.

Minimal: the edit changes only the jurisdiction words and the forum designation, converting non-exclusive to exclusive as the preferred element requires, and adds only the customary temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out that the element itself contemplates. Deletion of the redundant "laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia" phrase is part of the same choice-of-law selection, not an extraneous removal. No survival tails, fee-shifting, service-of-process, jury-waiver, or other boilerplate extras were added.

Preserves intent: the two-sentence structure, the scope phrase "All disputes under this Agreement," and the surrounding Section 20 boilerplate are retained; no undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence results, and no other allocation, timing, or remedy mechanic is disturbed.

Margin comment is compliant with tone: concise, first person plural, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the Delaware/California/England and Wales fallback without lecturing.
Fallback elements are marked not_met only because the preferred level was targeted; this does not affect position-completeness, which requires completion at either level.
